## Functions

### `async createRealmLocalSelectionHeadStorage(options)`

Bind one protected current-local-Realm selection and authority epoch to the captured operator account. Construction and reads never initialize storage. The epoch orders all selection changes for that account, including A-B-A, across Realm changes and source reopen; it is not a per-Realm reset counter. replaceCurrent accepts { localRealmId, advanceAuthority, expected, signal }. null selects no Realm by persisting a positive-epoch tombstone. Explicit advanceAuthority requires and retains the currently selected Realm. It invalidates earlier authority but grants no capability. Callers cannot supply/reset the next epoch. This is a kernel-only source, not a B4A port or a grant of Realm ownership, network access, traversal, Operations View, lifecycle, or activation. A future provider must bind policy/bake ownership and publish invalidation. It must also enforce kernel-controlled acquisition and isolate the protected backend before exposing app ports. A source import allowlist, view identity brand, or binding token alone cannot stop hostile same-origin native OPFS access. This source establishes no such runtime isolation boundary.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
